## 🌎 Geopolitics

### US Treasury sanctions Indian couple for helping Iran evade oil blockade, tightening "Operation Economic Outcast"

On November 4, the US Treasury Department sanctioned an Indian couple accused of supplying fake flag registrations to Iran's shadow fleet of oil tankers, circumventing international restrictions on Iranian crude exports. The move comes eight months after a June 2026 memorandum of understanding that paused US-Iran escalation and triggered a temporary sanctions waiver on Iranian oil. Treasury's action signals that despite the ceasefire framework, Washington is actively prosecuting enforcement against third-country facilitators of Iran's oil trade.

**Why it matters.** This directly touches India's energy security calculus. Russia already supplies 51% of India's crude (₹7.27 billion monthly as of July 2026), and now tighter Iran sanctions enforcement limits an alternative source. For a consulting practice tracking commodity flows or prop traders analyzing sanctions impact on crude futures, this signals the Trump administration is weaponizing financial infrastructure against circumvention schemes—a pattern that could escalate if congressional Democrats gain leverage in December's midterm carve-up. The targeting of Indian financial actors also hints at friction in the US-India trade relationship, which only just recovered from a 2025 diplomatic crisis.

**Action.** Watch Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) enforcement actions for additional Indian entities tied to Iran trade. Monitor Brent and WTI futures for spillover effects if Iran sanctions tighten further. Cross-reference with Chabahar port shipping data (Iran's gateway to India) and recent RBI guidance on rupee settlement of Iran trade to gauge how aggressively New Delhi will resist US pressure.

*Sources: [washingtontimes.com](https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2026/nov/4/treasury-department-sanctions-couple-accused-helping-iran-evade-oil/) · [theprint.in](https://theprint.in/economy/us-midterm-shake-up-cheaper-oil-for-india-but-tougher-russia-sanctions-could-complicate-crude-imports/3090792/)*

### Trump administration waives Russian diesel sanctions until April 2027, but eight tankers face legal limbo amid congressional override fight

On November 4, the Trump Treasury waived sanctions on Russian diesel imports through April 2027, opening the door for eight tankers carrying 300,000 tons of Russian fuel to dock in US ports between November 7 and 18. Four of the vessels—Leruo, Primorye, Manta, Feliks—are already sanctioned by the EU, UK, and Ukraine. New Jersey's governor immediately warned buyers that accepting the cargo may violate Congress's April 2022 ban on all Russian energy imports, arguing the Treasury lacks unilateral authority to override legislative prohibition. The legal standoff leaves shipowners and US port operators in immediate uncertainty.

**Why it matters.** This is a major geopolitical reversal with direct macro consequences. A sustained reopening of Russian energy to US markets would lower global crude prices—benefiting India's import bill and refiner margins—but also signals Trump's sanctions strategy diverges sharply from a Democratic Congress likely to reassert control after midterms. For prop traders and macro consultants, this creates a three-month arbitrage window (if the waiver holds) before April expiry, with enforcement risk priced in. The conflict between executive and legislative branches also foreshadows a broader sanctions policy reversal/tug-of-war if Democrats block further Russian sanctions relief.

**Action.** Follow November 7-18 for port-authority decisions and any OFAC enforcement action against the incoming tankers. Monitor crude price reactions and Russian ruble strength (a proxy for sanctions confidence). If the waiver survives, assume April 2027 becomes a hard deadline—position accordingly in front-month futures and look for US-EU sanctions divergence to widen, especially on Russian LNG, which could shift European energy flows toward India's LNG suppliers.

*Sources: [euromaidanpress.com](https://euromaidanpress.com/2026/11/04/300000-tons-of-russian-diesel-are-reportedly-heading-to-us-but-new-jersey-governor-warns-buyers-of-legal-risks) · [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/17/trump-eases-russia-oil-sanctions-but-is-europe-still-buying-moscows-gas)*

## 🧠 Artificial Intelligence

### GDPx Benchmark Shows Frontier Models Cap Out at 12% on Real Agentic Work

SemiAnalysis released GDPx on November 2, a benchmark spanning 206 tasks across 11 professional domains—chip design, cybersecurity, biology, finance, legal, quant trading, hardware design, materials science, alignment, software engineering, and recursive self-improvement. Claude Opus 5.5 leads the leaderboard at 12.0%, followed by Gemini 4 Carbon at 10.9% and GPT-6 Astra at 9.6%. This is intentionally a frontier-level benchmark; finance and legal tasks score zero under GDPx's binary grading scheme, revealing where safety classifiers constrain reasoning on real-world agentic tasks.

**Why it matters.** If you're building agentic systems, GDPx is the benchmark that matters. It measures what your system will actually fail at—not synthetic reasoning chains or multiple-choice, but compound domain work that requires planning, tool use, and iterative correction. The 12% ceiling on Claude Opus 5.5 signals that frontier models are still orders of magnitude away from reliable autonomous agents across professional domains. The zero-score domains (finance, legal) are particularly telling: safety layers are preventing the models from reasoning deep enough to solve complex problems. For production systems, this means accepting heavy human-in-the-loop workflows, or narrowing scope to domains where frontier models don't hit safety constraints.

**Action.** If your system targets cross-domain agentic capability, run GDPx (SemiAnalysis updates it every 3–6 months, so it won't stale like MMLU). Compare Claude Opus 5.5's 12% baseline against your target domain subset. Study the finance and legal breakdowns—those reveal the gap between what the model *could* reason through and what safety guardrails prevent. For production deployments, assume sub-12% success on novel frontier tasks and design human oversight accordingly.

*Sources: [[SemiAnalysis GDPx Benchmark Release](https://newsletter.semianalysis.com/p/gdpx-measuring-frontier-model-capabilities)]([SemiAnalysis GDPx Benchmark Release](https://newsletter.semianalysis.com/p/gdpx-measuring-frontier-model-capabilities)) · [[SemiAnalysis X Announcement](https://x.com/SemiAnalysis_/status/2117075900575477855)]([SemiAnalysis X Announcement](https://x.com/SemiAnalysis_/status/2117075900575477855)) · [[Unite.AI Coverage](https://www.unite.ai/semianalysis-launches-gdpx-benchmark-spanning-11-agentic-domains/)]([Unite.AI Coverage](https://www.unite.ai/semianalysis-launches-gdpx-benchmark-spanning-11-agentic-domains/))*

### Moonshot Publishes Kimi K3.1 Pro Weights—2.8T Open Model with 1M Context at $2/$10 Pricing

Moonshot AI shipped full model weights for Kimi K3.1 Pro on November 4 to Hugging Face (1.56 TB, MXFP4 quantized, ungated). The model has 2.8 trillion total parameters but only 104 billion active per token (mixture-of-experts), with a 1-million-token context window and text-plus-image input. On Terminal-Bench 4.0, Kimi K3.1 Pro scores 65.7%—ahead of GPT-6 Astra (58.2%) and within 0.7 points of Claude Opus 5.5 (66.4%). Pricing via Moonshot's API is $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output—roughly a third the cost of Kimi K3.

**Why it matters.** This is a genuinely competitive open-weight model with the context window and throughput to handle multi-document reasoning at price points that undercut closed APIs. For engineers building cost-sensitive systems—especially in regions where API access is restricted or latency-critical—Kimi K3.1 Pro is no longer a second-tier fallback. The MoE architecture (only 104B active) means you can serve it efficiently on modest hardware; the 1M context lets you reason over 200-page documents in a single forward pass. Moonshot's preprocessing decision to strip cyberattack-related material before open-source release signals that labs are thinking about responsible disclosure in weight releases. The license (MIT-style for sub-$20M-revenue companies, paid agreement required above that) is straightforward for production use.

**Action.** If you're operating in high-latency or cost-constrained environments, benchmark Kimi K3.1 Pro against Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra on your eval set—Terminal-Bench is public, but your own domain tests will tell you if the 0.7% gap matters. For local deployment, reserve 8× NVIDIA B300 GPUs (2.3 TB VRAM) for inference; the MoE design makes it feasible for privacy-sensitive workloads. Check the license agreement if you plan to offer it as a service—hosted revenue above $20M will require negotiation with Moonshot.

*Sources: [[Moonshot Kimi K3.1 Pro Release](https://x.com/AndrewCurran_/status/2118008152474222701)]([Moonshot Kimi K3.1 Pro Release](https://x.com/AndrewCurran_/status/2118008152474222701)) · [[Startup Fortune](https://startupfortune.com/moonshot-ai-releases-full-weights-for-28-trillion-parameter-kimi-k31-pro/)]([Startup Fortune](https://startupfortune.com/moonshot-ai-releases-full-weights-for-28-trillion-parameter-kimi-k31-pro/)) · [[AI-TLDR](https://ai-tldr.dev/releases/moonshot-kimi-k3-1-pro-open-weights/)]([AI-TLDR](https://ai-tldr.dev/releases/moonshot-kimi-k3-1-pro-open-weights/))*

## 🇮🇳 India

### Razorpay wins SEBI approval for ₹6,000 crore IPO, targets Q1 2027 listing

Razorpay, India's largest payments infrastructure platform, has received SEBI approval for its initial public offering with a fundraise target of ₹5,000–6,000 crore. The fintech unicorn plans to list on Indian exchanges in Q1 2027, ending years of speculation around its public debut timing and marking a major validation of India's payments-tech maturity.

**Why it matters.** Razorpay's SEBI nod unlocks ₹5,000–6,000 crore in founder wealth and LP capital that will immediately recycle into hiring, deep-tech investment, and downstream fintech rounds. For AI engineers in Hyderabad or Bangalore building payments, lending, or financial services tools, this sets the market valuation ceiling for exits—comparable startups now know what institutional returns look like. The approval also signals to global LPs that India's fintech infrastructure layer is mature enough for public markets, thawing fundraising sentiment across B2B SaaS, embedded finance, and AI-led lending.

**Action.** Pull Razorpay's DRHP (draft red herring prospectus) from BSE and NSE websites once filed to review cap table, revenue metrics, and margin trends. Track SEBI's published list of pending IPO approvals (110+ companies awaited nod as of November); Razorpay's success will accelerate timelines for peers. If recruiting, watch for insider selling windows post-listing (typically 6–12 months) when founders and employees liquidate and rejoin the ecosystem.

*Sources: [[Inc42 (Nov 4, 2026)](https://inc42.com/)]([Inc42 (Nov 4, 2026)](https://inc42.com/)) · [[StartupTalky Daily Roundup](https://startuptalky.com/news/daily-indian-funding-roundup-key-news-4-november-2026/)]([StartupTalky Daily Roundup](https://startuptalky.com/news/daily-indian-funding-roundup-key-news-4-november-2026/))*

### NPCI launches AI and blockchain subsidiary, expanding beyond payments rail

The National Payments Corporation of India—operator of India's entire digital payments backbone (UPI, RuPay, AADHAR Pay)—has established a new subsidiary focused on artificial intelligence and blockchain technologies. The move signals RBI's mandate to embed AI into core financial infrastructure and represents NPCI's first structural pivot toward research and innovation beyond payments settlement.

**Why it matters.** NPCI has historically treated infrastructure innovation as secondary; this subsidiary reverses that posture and opens procurement, hiring, and contract cycles for startups building AI fraud detection, transaction intelligence, or blockchain settlement tools. For AI engineers considering fintech careers: NPCI roles now come with access to India's complete payments dataset and direct mandate from the central bank—a structural advantage over private fintech employers. Early hires will shape RBI's AI infrastructure policy and set precedent for public-sector tech hiring at scale.

**Action.** Check rbi.org.in and npci.org.in for the subsidiary's governance structure, leadership, and initial roadmap. Watch for job postings and RFP announcements targeting AI, fraud detection, or blockchain capabilities. If you're at an AI fintech startup, contact the subsidiary's business development team once contact details surface—they represent a new class of enterprise customer with direct central-bank backing and unlimited procurement authority for infrastructure services.

## 💹 Global Stocks

### MSFT (NASDAQ): +6.7% to $555.80 on Q1 FY2027 earnings beat, Azure accelerates

Microsoft closed at $555.80 on November 4, up 6.7%, after fiscal first-quarter results exceeded expectations across the board. Revenue hit $92.28 billion, beating consensus of $90.62 billion by 1.8% year-over-year growth of 19%. Adjusted EPS of $4.92 surpassed the $4.71 consensus estimate. Azure infrastructure revenue expanded 48%, a material acceleration that signaled AI capex demand remains healthy despite broader macro uncertainty.

**Why it matters.** Azure's 48% growth directly reflects enterprise commitment to AI infrastructure spending. For engineers and investors tracking the semiconductor and AI spending cycle, this is a bellwether: the largest cloud operator's acceleration suggests the data-center build-out is not slowing, which supports the entire AI chip ecosystem—a reassurance after October's Intel implosion. Microsoft's strength also implies that even if policy shifts (as the midterm election results now pose), established players with existing capex commitments are insulated. This read-across matters for TSM, ASML, and semis supply-chain names watching visibility into 2027.

**Action.** Review the full Q1 FY2027 earnings transcript filed with the SEC (look for Azure pricing pressure and guidance confidence). Microsoft guided Q2 FY2027 revenue to $96.0–$97.1 billion; watch that range in the next quarter to gauge either acceleration or normalization. Cloud gross margin dropped to 66%, a metric worth monitoring for margin sustainability.

*Sources: [[Microsoft Investor Relations Q1 FY2027 Earnings](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/investor/events/fy-2027/earnings-fy-2027-q1)]([Microsoft Investor Relations Q1 FY2027 Earnings](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/investor/events/fy-2027/earnings-fy-2027-q1)) · [[CNBC Microsoft Q1 2027 Earnings](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/28/microsoft-msft-q1-earnings-report-2027.html)]([CNBC Microsoft Q1 2027 Earnings](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/28/microsoft-msft-q1-earnings-report-2027.html)) · [[Tickeron MSFT FY2027 Q1 Recap](https://tickeron.com/earnings/MSFT/)]([Tickeron MSFT FY2027 Q1 Recap](https://tickeron.com/earnings/MSFT/))*

### NVDA (NASDAQ): -3.2% to $200.13 on midterm election data-center delay concerns

Nvidia closed at $200.13 on November 4, down 3.17%, as the chip sector sold off sharply after the midterm election results sparked investor concern over political resistance to AI infrastructure expansion. The decline ran counter to a broader Nasdaq rally, with Asian chip peers hit even harder. Specific trigger: reports of potential delays to data-center power projects in Texas, signaling regulatory and political headwinds for hyperscaler capex plans.

**Why it matters.** This move isolates real political and infrastructure risk to the AI buildout narrative. Unlike valuation or earnings revisions, regulatory opposition to energy-intensive data centers poses asymmetric downside to the semis cycle itself. For Nvidia specifically, it complicates the post-earnings story: the company guides China revenue out of its forward guidance, so if US infrastructure capex also faces delays, the addressable market for high-end accelerators shrinks materially. This has read-across to ASML, TSM, and power/cooling equipment makers, where the political backdrop now matters as much as demand growth.

**Action.** Monitor the next earnings call on November 17, 2026; listen closely for any language on US data-center visibility, capex cycle confidence, and guidance adjustments. Watch insider selling activity—the stock has seen ~$399 million in recent insider sales, a sentiment red flag. Key levels: $200 support and the $210–$215 range as near-term resistance.

## 🏗 Tech & Startups

### Marvell and Lumentum Merge in $115 Billion Chipmaking Consolidation

Semiconductor giant Marvell Technology agreed to combine with optical component maker Lumentum Holdings in a transaction valued at approximately $115 billion, announced November 2. The deal marks the largest tech M&A of the year involving semiconductor players and signals intensifying consolidation in foundational chip infrastructure as AI and data-center demand surge globally.

**Why it matters.** The merger reflects a playbook now standard in semiconductor strategy: integrate vertically to control both logic and optical interconnect in a single supply chain. For founders in chipmaking, photonics, or adjacent deeptech, this signals that standalone suppliers face pressure to consolidate or risk losing tier-one customers to vertically integrated competitors. The deal also underscores AI infrastructure capex flowing toward silicon—not just software.

**Action.** Track the merger's regulatory timeline (US CFIUS and international antitrust reviews will take months). Watch for which customers push back on cross-licensing or sole-sourcing concerns. Subscribe to Marvell's investor relations updates to see post-close integration strategy—they'll likely announce consolidation at manufacturing or R&D levels.

### Agility Robotics Clears SPAC Merger, Debuts on Nasdaq Today

Agility Robotics, the Portland-based humanoid robot company, received shareholder approval for its merger with Churchill Capital Corp XI on November 2, clearing the path for a Nasdaq listing on November 5. The deal brings Agility $465 million in capital at a time when corporate demand for logistics automation intensifies and robotics supply chains mature.

**Why it matters.** Agility's public listing validates the deeptech robotics sector for public markets—not a software IPO, but a capital-intensive hardware play backed by serious capital. For founders building commercial robots or robotics infrastructure, this signals that profitable unit economics and credible customer traction (Agility has FedEx, BMW, and others) can sustain valuations through public scrutiny. The SPAC route also shows an alternative to traditional IPO timelines when you need cash runway.

**Action.** Watch Agility's first earnings call for customer concentration and gross margins. Check whether other humanoid or logistics robotics startups accelerate IPO or SPAC timelines in response. Follow Agility's supply-chain partnerships—their manufacturing and component sourcing strategy will shape which robotics subsystem plays attract follow-on funding.

## 🩹 Health & Science

### FDA Approves Hibsago (Bepirovirsen), First "Functional Cure" for Chronic Hepatitis B

GlaxoSmithKline's bepirovirsen received FDA approval on November 5, 2026, marking the first treatment to achieve a "functional cure" in chronic hepatitis B—suppressing the virus to undetectable levels in blood and maintaining that suppression after treatment stops. The approval is based on two Phase 3 trials published in the *New England Journal of Medicine*: 233 of 1,220 treated participants reached functional cure versus 0 of 614 on placebo (19.1% efficacy rate with sustained viral suppression). Treatment duration is 48 weeks.

**Why it matters.** Approximately 290 million people globally carry chronic hepatitis B, most with limited options beyond antivirals that suppress but don't cure the virus. A functional cure would be the first durable, off-therapy outcome for the disease, representing a genuine clinical inflection. For builders in viral immunotherapy and RNA-targeting platforms, this validates the functional cure pathway as clinically achievable and commercially viable.

**Action.** Read the Phase 3 trial data in NEJM (search "bepirovirsen hepatitis B phase 3"). For therapeutics teams, the specific mechanism—antisense oligonucleotide targeting hepatitis B surface antigen—offers a template for other persistent viral infections (HCV in certain populations, HTLV-1). The pricing and insurance reimbursement will set precedent for the "functional cure" category; monitor Gilead's response in their own hepatitis B pipeline.

*Sources: [[ScienceAlert — FDA Approves First Drug Offering a 'Functional Cure' For Chronic Hepatitis B](https://www.sciencealert.com/breakthrough-fda-approves-first-drug-offering-a-functional-cure-for-chronic-hepatitis-b)]([ScienceAlert — FDA Approves First Drug Offering a 'Functional Cure' For Chronic Hepatitis B](https://www.sciencealert.com/breakthrough-fda-approves-first-drug-offering-a-functional-cure-for-chronic-hepatitis-b)) · [[Yahoo News — Hibsago approval and trial data](https://www.yahoo.com/news/science/articles/breakthrough-fda-approves-first-drug-offering-a-functional-cure-for-chronic-hepatitis-b-030000981.html)]([Yahoo News — Hibsago approval and trial data](https://www.yahoo.com/news/science/articles/breakthrough-fda-approves-first-drug-offering-a-functional-cure-for-chronic-hepatitis-b-030000981.html))*

## 🎤 Culture & World

### Godzilla Minus Zero Opens North America This Week, Staking Japan's Claim on Monster Mythology

Takashi Yamazaki's Godzilla Minus Zero arrives in North American theaters November 6, 2026, two days after its November 3 premiere in Japan on Godzilla Day. The film sets the story two years after the massive hit Godzilla Minus One and is distributed by GKIDS. Yamazaki returns as director, screenwriter, and VFX supervisor. Box Office Pro forecasts a domestic opening weekend of $25–$50 million, directly competing against The Cat in the Hat's animated adaptation.

**Why it matters.** This is theatrical distribution betting on Japanese monster cinema as a global franchise. Godzilla Minus One became a cultural phenomenon and the highest-grossing anime film ever; Minus Zero doubles down on that momentum by keeping creative control with Yamazaki rather than handing it to Hollywood. The November 3 Japan-first premiere (the anniversary of the 1954 original) signals reclaiming Godzilla as explicitly Japanese intellectual property at a time when American studios typically dominate both production and theatrical windows. For streamers and studios, this is a test of whether subtitled live-action anime-adjacent films can sustain box office beyond opening weekends.

**Action.** Watch the opening-weekend box office split between Minus Zero and The Cat in the Hat. If Minus Zero overperforms—especially among adults and international audiences—expect more Japanese creators to bypass Hollywood gatekeeping for high-budget theatrical releases. Track whether GKIDS's distribution reach (indie studio, not major conglomerate) attracts prestige reviewers and whether Minus Zero sustains legs into week two, signaling whether audiences will return for sequels.

*Sources: [[godzilla.com](https://godzilla.com/blogs/news/godzilla-minus-zero-confirmed-for-north-american-theatrical-release-on-november-6)]([godzilla.com](https://godzilla.com/blogs/news/godzilla-minus-zero-confirmed-for-north-american-theatrical-release-on-november-6)) · [[Hypebeast](https://hypebeast.com/2026/1/toho-studios-godzilla-minus-zero-november-2026-release-info)]([Hypebeast](https://hypebeast.com/2026/1/toho-studios-godzilla-minus-zero-november-2026-release-info)) · [[Box Office Pro](https://www.boxofficepro.com/long-range-forecast-monsters-make-their-way-to-the-big-screen-in-the-cat-in-the-hat-godzilla-minus-zero/)]([Box Office Pro](https://www.boxofficepro.com/long-range-forecast-monsters-make-their-way-to-the-big-screen-in-the-cat-in-the-hat-godzilla-minus-zero/))*

### The Rings of Power Season 3 Launches November 11: Amazon's Middle-earth Strategy Enters Make-or-Break Year

The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3 premieres on Prime Video November 11, 2026, with four episodes on day one, two more November 18, and the final two November 25. The season follows Sauron's quest to forge the One Ring amid the War of the Elves and Sauron. Amazon has already renewed the show for Season 4, signaling confidence in the IP as a multi-year anchor for Prime Video. The ensemble cast includes returning performances from Rory Kinnear as Tom Bombadil and new voice work from Simon Pegg as the Balrog of Moria.

**Why it matters.** Prime Video is weaponizing Tolkien as a tentpole streaming anchor in a congested market. By staggering episode releases across three weeks (a strategy Netflix perfected with Stranger Things), Amazon forces sustained engagement and shapes the cultural conversation across the holiday season. The show costs roughly $1 billion for three seasons, making it one of the most expensive television productions ever; Season 4's greenlight before Season 3's premiere indicates Amazon believes the long-tail viewership justifies the spend. For the streaming wars, this is evidence that prestige fantasy with a recognizable IP moat can still justify eight-figure per-episode budgets, even as Netflix pivots to cheaper procedurals.

**Action.** Track Prime Video's reported viewership metrics for the premiere week—Amazon rarely discloses numbers, but if they do, it signals confidence. Watch whether Season 3 sustains the fandom momentum from Seasons 1 and 2 or if critical reception splinters the audience. The November stagger puts the finale at Thanksgiving 2026; monitor whether that creates appointment viewing behavior or if the three-week gap causes churn to competitors.

*Sources: [[3dvf](https://3dvf.com/en/the-rings-of-power-season-3-sets-prime-video-release-for-nov-11-2026/)]([3dvf](https://3dvf.com/en/the-rings-of-power-season-3-sets-prime-video-release-for-nov-11-2026/)) · [[The Statesman](https://www.thestatesman.com/entertainment/ott/the-lord-of-the-rings-the-rings-of-power-season-3-release-date-amazon-prime-video-november-release-date-november-1503592821.html)]([The Statesman](https://www.thestatesman.com/entertainment/ott/the-lord-of-the-rings-the-rings-of-power-season-3-release-date-amazon-prime-video-november-release-date-november-1503592821.html)) · [[The Onering.net](https://www.theonering.net/torwp/2026/05/11/121807-rings-of-power-season-3-release-date-confirmed-for-november-11-on-prime-video/)]([The Onering.net](https://www.theonering.net/torwp/2026/05/11/121807-rings-of-power-season-3-release-date-confirmed-for-november-11-on-prime-video/))*
